subject.title: Feature Request: One-click Anthropic authentication (OAuth flow)

question: Should OpenClaw pursue a first-class Anthropic browser OAuth onboarding flow, or should Anthropic subscription setup stay on the supported Claude CLI/setup-token paths until Anthropic grants a clearer third-party product contract?
rationale: The code has an internal OAuth helper but no exposed Anthropic OAuth auth choice, and official Anthropic guidance makes third-party Claude.ai OAuth use a product/security boundary rather than a narrow implementation gap.

options.title: Keep open for product/security design
options.body: Define the permitted Anthropic auth contract, scopes, callback behavior, token storage, and account/billing UX before queueing implementation.

options.title: Narrow to Claude CLI/setup-token UX
options.body: Treat one-click OAuth as out of scope for now and improve the current supported paths with clearer onboarding copy, token-prefix detection, or Claude CLI setup guidance.

options.title: Decline browser OAuth
options.body: Close the full browser OAuth direction unless Anthropic provides explicit permission or a supported public API contract for OpenClaw's use case.

recommendation.title: Keep open for product/security design
recommendation.body: Define the permitted Anthropic auth contract, scopes, callback behavior, token storage, and account/billing UX before queueing implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Current source provenance points to this area, and the decision crosses Anthropic provider auth, security posture, and onboarding UX.
